items.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: He had Firehouse Five, and Louis Armstrong and various things. So that’s what got my brother and I all fired up about Hot music.

ctx.x: Yeah. And also Thelonious Monk Jr. was there and I started doing some playing with him, in fact I played the bass sax with his — oh it was a tentet I think they had, playing the music of Monk. So we just went around and talked a little bit about how we got involved in jazz and all of that. And of course in most cases it does come through the family somehow. You know our father had old ‘78s. How many times have you heard that story? We listened to dad’s ‘78s and got all excited about the music. There you go. ©…
He had Firehouse Five, and Louis Armstrong and various things. So that’s what got my brother and I all fired up about Hot music.
Do you have an opinion on the racial state of jazz these days? I think of it when I’m at a function like this, that the audience is all white and —
